newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity futures ease in bearish mood.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity futures ease in bearish mood.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures eased Thursday in a bearish mood set by the return to service of generation units in the U.S. West and below normal temperatures in the Pacific Northwest, industry sources said.
Lower natural gas prices were also putting some psychological pressure on power futures, the sources said.

As of 1220 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) futures were trading down 93 cents at $33.40 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $33.00-33.75, while September had traded down 54 cents at $28.70 after trades in a range of $28.60-29.10 per MWh.
August California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were down 35 cents at the day's high of $22.75 after exchange as low as $22.50, while September had traded down 25 cents at $22.70 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 51 COB and 275 PV contracts had traded.

Temperatures through the Pacific Northwest were forecast to be cooler-than-normal into early next week, while the Southwest was expected to see temperatures one to three degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the south and west and near normal elsewhere over the next several days.
The 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 2 nuclear power unit in Arizona reached 98 percent power early Thursday after dropping to 60 percent due to a low pressure feedwater heater outage.
Also scheduled to return to service shortly were the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state and 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in southern California.

Several Western coal-fired power units were expected to return to the power grid beginning today, including a 300 MW Reid Gardner unit in Las Vegas, Nevada, a 670 MW unit at Centralia, Wash., a 330 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado.
As of 1220 EDT, August NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 6.3 cents at $2.15 per million British thermal units.
COB open interest for June 25 fell 229 to 6,574, while PV open interest rose 36 to 6,393, NYMEX said.
